# Frozen execution fixtures

These files are offline functional inputs, not live-chain captures or performance results.

The `evm-*` and `wbft-*` fixtures come from the isolated [StableNet executor](../../x/stablenet/executor/README.md), whose EVM/WBFT replay and bootstrap contracts remain unchanged.

The five `arc-*.json` files are generated by the official [Arc executor libraries](../../x/arc/executor/README.md) pinned to `6e764023ee6515fe70573e123ed2db912a7207b4`. They use a **synthetic chain ID 1337/anchor**, derived from the pinned local-development allocation plus public test accounts/contracts. They are not Arc testnet/mainnet genesis or operational checkpoints. Transactions use the public Alloy test signature; no private key is included. The fixture records the source revision, complete synthetic baseline, original parent header, verified EXR1 bytes and expected public state. Arc allocation bytecode is redistributed under the included [Apache-2.0 license](arc-LICENSE.txt); upstream copyright is Circle Internet Group, Inc. Contract dependencies retain their upstream notices in the linked source repository.

`arc-storage` and `arc-create-gone` cover ordinary replay and creation/destruction. `arc-calls` and `evm-calls` exercise all seven native call kinds and reverted ancestors. `arc-call-from-direct` keeps the physical transaction root separate from its logical precompile call. `arc-call-from-oog` covers a successful logical child whose result completion subsequently fails and rolls its state back while its caller succeeds. These are reproducible call-hook fixtures; they do not prove live peer coverage or cryptographically commit every child call. See the [native call contract](../../docs/EXECUTION_CALL_TRACES.md).

Reproduce into an owned temporary directory and compare, without updating fixtures implicitly:

```sh
cd x/arc/executor
INDEXER_ARC_FIXTURE_DIR=/YOUR_OWNED_TEMP_DIRECTORY cargo test --locked --lib tests::frozen_arc_consumer_fixtures_are_reproducible -- --exact
```

The Go app tests independently decode the raw block/body/receipt commitments and exercise the actual disposable PostgreSQL publication/API path. Native library tests independently reconstruct intermediate journal roots and reject omissions/corruption. No node service or live RPC is required.

`arc-native-checkpoint.ndjson` is the pinned LOCAL_DEV genesis (chain1337) exported by the native Rust checkpoint writer and independently verified in Go. It is not a mainnet/testnet operational anchor. Regenerate with `INDEXER_ARC_FIXTURE_DIR=/YOUR_OWNED_TEMP_DIRECTORY cargo test --locked --lib native_checkpoint_full_root_and_missing_key_coverage`; CI compares bytes. The included Arc license also covers allocation code in this fixture.

`evm-blobs.json` is generated by the isolated recorder from signed type-3 references and actual Cancun EVM/pre-block replay. It includes EIP-4788 system state changes and a synthetic PoS genesis/empty withdrawals, with original node state preserved. It deliberately contains no sidecar bundle: tests compose independently known zero-polynomial full-blob proofs before spool admission. It is not a live-chain checkpoint, beacon inclusion or finality proof.
